title: Hand-eye calibrate both of a robot's wrist cameras against a ChArUco board on the bench
instruction: Hand-eye calibrate both wrist cameras with the ChArUco board on the bench, then take both arms back to where they started.
context: A robot that grasps what its wrist cameras see needs each camera's exact pose on its gripper, its hand-eye calibration. It is measured when the robot is built, and again whenever a camera is remounted or knocked. In the standard eye-in-hand procedure (MoveIt Calibration, easy_handeye, OpenCV's calibrateHandEye) the board stays put and each arm moves its own camera round it, stopping at a dozen or more well-spread poses with the whole board in view. Today a person drives each arm through those poses, robot by robot.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. (1) Book stand, fixed: beech; a base 17.8 cm deep (x 35.8 to 53.6) and 30 cm wide (y -15 to 15), 1.2 cm thick; a lip 1 cm tall and 0.8 cm thick across its front (x 36.6 to 37.4); a sloped rest 26 cm wide and 14.5 cm long under the board's back, held at its upper end by a block (x 49.4 to 52.6, 11 cm tall). (2) ChArUco calibration board, loose, leaning back 45 degrees from upright on the stand with its printed face toward the arms: an A4 plate (29.7 x 21 cm, landscape), 3 mm aluminium composite, 0.24 kg, its bottom edge on the stand's base against the lip (the edge's middle at x 38, y 0), its middle at x 45.4, 8.7 cm up, its top edge 16.2 cm up. Printed in its middle: a ChArUco board of 7 x 5 black and white squares of 3 cm (21 x 15 cm; 24 inner corners), with a 2.2 cm ArUco marker in each of the 17 white squares (OpenCV dictionary DICT_5X5_250, ids 0 to 16), as OpenCV's CharucoBoard draws it. Its back is grey. (3) The wrist cameras: one on each gripper's side, 7 cm out from the gripper's axis and 7.3 cm along it, looking out along the fingers and turned 25 degrees in toward them (the station's calibrated mounts); 1280 x 720 pixels, focal length 781 pixels (78 degrees across). The arms start at their home pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The board's pose is read from the simulation, each arm's joints and gripper pose from the robot. What each wrist camera sees of the board is computed from the camera's pose and its intrinsics, and OpenCV's ChArUco detector is run on that frame. A camera's sample is taken automatically when the whole print is 8 pixels or more inside the frame, no part of either arm or the stand is in front of it as seen from the camera, its image has moved under 2 pixels in the last 0.5 s, the camera is turned 15 degrees or more from every earlier sample of that camera, and the detector finds all 24 corners. A sample is the gripper's pose in its arm's base frame (from the joint angles) with the board's pose in the camera (OpenCV's solvePnP). Per camera: 0.05 per sample, up to 12 (0.6); +0.1 once two rotations between its samples of 30 degrees or more have axes 45 degrees or more apart; +0.1 once it has 12 or more samples, that holds, and OpenCV's calibrateHandEye (Park's method) on all its samples puts the camera within 5 mm and 1 degree of its true mount. Score: the mean of the two cameras' scores (at most 0.8). 1.0: both cameras calibrated, the board moved under 1 mm from where it settled, both arms back at their start (each fingertip centre within 5 cm) and still, for 1 s. 0 for the rest of the run once the board moves more than 2 mm or any part of an arm comes within 2 mm of it. Doing nothing scores 0. With real parts, the robot logs its joint angles and both wrist cameras record; the same detector and calibrateHandEye are run on the log and compared with a reference calibration.
reset_notes: Lean the board on the stand, printed face toward the arms, its bottom edge against the lip, as in the screenshot; arms at home. Nothing is consumed. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz; board, stand and cameras at true size. The cameras' frames for the calibration are drawn from each camera's pose with the station's calibrated lens at 1280 x 720 (ideal pinhole: no distortion, blur or lighting) for OpenCV's ChArUco detector; the arms are boxes round their links and fingers for the line-of-sight and touch tests. A sample is taken automatically when the camera is held still, in place of a "take sample" click.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it drew both arms back toward their bases, raised them toward the board once and lowered them again; neither camera ever held the whole board in view while still, so no sample was taken); demo: 1.0
